generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a rootless bromeliad of the south-eastern United States and tropical America that hangs in grey festoons up to a few metres long from the branches of live oaks and cypresses, its thread-like stems and scales silvered with absorbing hairs; it spreads by fragments and seed carried by the wind. On the Oregon white oak here as a stand-in for a live oak. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: festoons reaching about 12 m up its host's crown at 20 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: silver-grey strands.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
